facts.text: On this date in 1991, hikers discovered Ötzi the Iceman in the Alps — but initially reported him to Austrian authorities. The body actually lay in Italian territory, a boundary only confirmed by GPS survey four years later.

On this date in 1955, Argentina's President Perón was ousted by a military coup and fled to Paraguay. He returned 18 years later, won the presidency again, and died in office — the only leader to hold power across such a gap.
More people live inside a circle drawn 4,000 km around Dhaka, Bangladesh than live outside it. That single radius captures roughly half of all humanity.
The city of Chongqing, China, has more residents than Australia, Canada, and the Netherlands combined — yet most Westerners cannot locate it on a map.
Monaco is so densely populated that if the entire United States held the same density, its population would exceed 40 trillion people — more than 5,000 times every human who has ever lived.
On this date in 1873, Jay Cooke & Company collapsed, triggering a US bank panic so severe that the New York Stock Exchange closed for 10 days — still the longest shutdown in its history.
On September 19, 2008, the SEC temporarily banned short-selling on 799 financial stocks. The affected shares fell harder than the broader market once the ban lifted.
The entire global bond market is roughly $130 trillion — about 1.3 times the size of global GDP, and nearly three times larger than all stock markets combined.
Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway collects so much cash from insurance float that it essentially borrows billions at negative cost, then invests it at full return.
The tulip mania peak of 1637 is routinely overstated — most Dutch never traded bulbs. The actual market was small, illiquid, and collapsed in a single February weekend.
On this date in 1988, Israel launched its first satellite, Ofeq-1 — orbiting west-to-east against Earth's rotation to avoid debris from its own rocket falling on neighboring countries.
On September 19, 1991, hikers discovered Ötzi the Iceman in the Alps. His last meal, eaten an hour before he was murdered, included ibex, einkorn wheat, and red deer.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its matter would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Your body replaces the lining of your stomach every four to five days — it has to, or your digestive acid would dissolve the organ itself.
Voyager 1 is so far away that its radio signals, traveling at the speed of light, take over 22 hours to reach Earth. It left the solar system before most people working at NASA today were born.
On this day in 1991, hikers discovered Ötzi the Iceman in the Alps — a man who died 5,300 years ago, older than Stonehenge and the Egyptian pyramids.
On this day in 1783, the Montgolfier brothers launched history's first balloon passengers: a sheep, a duck, and a rooster.
The fax machine was patented in 1843 — 23 years before the first transatlantic telegraph cable worked, and 44 years before the telephone reached mass use.
Oxford University was teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. Oxford dates to 1096; Tenochtitlán wasn't founded until 1325.
Nintendo was founded in 1889, when Grover Cleveland was U.S. president. It spent its first century selling playing cards before pivoting to video games.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012 — too precise to stay invented.
Hiraeth (n.): a Welsh longing for a home that may never have existed. The word fuses homesickness, grief, and nostalgia into a single sound English has never managed to replicate.
On this day in 1796, Washington's Farewell Address was published — introducing 'entangling alliances' to the political lexicon, a phrase Jefferson actually sharpened before it became doctrine.

Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word from Tierra del Fuego meaning a look shared by two people who both wish the other would initiate something. Linguists call it one of the most succinct words ever recorded.
On this day in 1783, the Montgolfier brothers' balloon carried its first passengers — a sheep, a duck, and a rooster — before French acquired the word 'aéronaute' to describe the humans who followed.

On this date in 2017, China's central bank declared ICOs illegal and ordered all fundraised funds returned — wiping out billions in token valuations within 48 hours and accelerating the migration of Chinese crypto firms to Hong Kong and Singapore.

On this date in 2022, Ethereum completed The Merge, switching from proof-of-work to proof-of-stake and cutting the network's energy consumption by approximately 99.95% — without halting a single block.

Bitcoin's 21 million supply cap is enforced by code, not consensus: a 2010 overflow bug briefly created 184 billion BTC in one transaction before Satoshi patched it within hours and the chain was manually rolled back.

The gas limit on Ethereum is not fixed — it's a moving average adjusted block-by-block based on miner and validator votes, meaning the network's throughput capacity is continuously negotiated in real time.

Satoshi Nakamoto's known wallets hold roughly 1.1 million BTC that have never moved — making them the most-watched addresses in financial history and a de facto proof-of-life signal for Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator.

On this date in 2017, Libratus—a Carnegie Mellon poker AI—had already finished its 20-day demolition of four top human heads-up no-limit Texas Hold'em players, winning $1.77M in chips. It invented bluffing strategies its creators had never programmed.

On this date in 2022, papers confirming Gato's existence were four months old. DeepMind's 1.2B-parameter generalist agent played Atari, captioned images, and stacked real blocks—same weights, no task-specific fine-tuning.

The GPT-4 training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 GWh of electricity—enough to power about 4,600 average US homes for a year. That figure predates inference costs, which now dwarf training at scale.

Transformers have no built-in notion of sequence order. Positional encodings are a retrofit—an acknowledgment that the attention mechanism itself is entirely permutation-invariant and would treat a sentence the same forwards or backwards without them.

AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for ~200 million proteins in 2022. The entire prior corpus of experimentally determined structures, accumulated over 50 years of crystallography and NMR work, covered roughly 180,000.
